title: Design System: Renal Relay care-team workspace

components.name: Primary Action
components.description: 40px teal action with clear disabled state.
components.css: .ds-primary { min-height: 40px; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; background: #087f78; padding: 0 14px; color: #fff; font: 600 14px/1.5 Geist, Arial, sans-serif; } .ds-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #39a99d; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-primary:disabled { cursor: not-allowed; opacity: .62; }

components.name: Episode Data Surface
components.description: White, thin-bordered 12px surface; no persistent shadow.

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: Pale teal workflow state with an explicit text label.
components.css: .ds-status { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; border-radius: 999px; background: #eaf5f3; padding: 5px 8px; color: #086660; font: 600 10px/1.4 Geist, Arial, sans-serif; } .ds-status > span { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; background: #168378; }

narrative.northStar: Care-team follow-through made visible, legible, and accountable.
narrative.overview: A calm light workspace gives episode state, due dates, owners, and next steps precedence. Neutral surfaces dominate; teal organizes navigation and primary actions. The dashboard is the first implemented surface, and all displayed sample records are fictional.
keyCharacteristics: Fixed desktop navigation rail and constrained operational content column.
Episode table with status, ordered tests, due date, and named owner.
Flat neutral surfaces with teal accents and restrained warning color.
Responsive horizontal navigation and horizontally scrollable data table on small screens.
rules: Pair every state color with a readable text label.
Keep episode status, due date, owner, and next step easy to scan.
Use borders and spacing for persistent grouping; reserve shadows for overlays.
Label fictional demonstration data wherever it could be mistaken for live records.
dos: Do use teal as a purposeful interaction accent on quiet neutral surfaces.
Do keep clinical authority and decision-making with the care team.
Do provide keyboard focus and semantic structure.
donts: Don't imply real patient data, health-system connectivity, or automated clinical decisions.
Don't use color alone to convey status.
Don't use decorative charts or gradients in place of actionable episode information.
